title: No-prime spec inequality as a calc-chain through the central binomial (2n n)
intent: Reduce the goal "if no prime lies between n and 2n then power 4 n < power (2*n) (div (sqr (2*n)) 2) * power 4 (div (2*n) 3)" to two bound lemmas on the central binomial `binomial (2*n) n` — the lower bound `binomial_even` and the upper bound `upper_bound` — and chain them through `2 * n * binomial (2*n) n` with `Nat.le_lt_trans` and `Nat.lt_le_trans`.

parent.name: no_prime_imp_spec_inegality
parent.statement:
Theorem no_prime_imp_spec_inegality :
 forall n : nat,
 power 2 7 <= n ->
 (forall p : nat, n < p -> p < 2 * n -> ~ prime p) ->
 power 4 n < power (2 * n) (div (sqr (2 * n)) 2) * power 4 (div (2 * n) 3).

children.name: upper_bound
children.statement:
Theorem upper_bound :
 forall n : nat,
 power 2 7 <= n ->
 (forall p : nat, n < p -> p < 2 * n -> ~ prime p) ->
 binomial (2 * n) n <
 power (2 * n) (div (sqr (2 * n)) 2 - 1) * power 4 (div (2 * n) 3).
children.closed_by: its own 158-line calc-chain: factorize binomial (2*n) n with `factorization` (Bertrand.v line 41), split the product with `prod_nm_split`, then chain `Nat.lt_le_trans`/`Nat.le_lt_trans` through `prod_nm 0 (div (2*n) 3) ...` and close each prime-power bound with `power_div_binomial1/2/3`, `prod_prime_lt`, `prod_prime_le`
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: binomial (2*n) n is bounded above by power (2*n) (div (sqr (2*n)) 2 - 1) * power 4 (div (2*n) 3), under the same no-prime and n-large hypotheses

children.name: binomial_even
children.statement:
Theorem binomial_even :
 forall n : nat, 0 < n -> power 2 (2 * n) <= 2 * n * binomial (2 * n) n.
children.closed_by: rewrites `binomial2` (Binomial.v line 271), splits the sum with `sum_nm_split`, reduces the bound to `binomial_mono`/`binomial_comp`/`binomial_def3`/`binomial_def4`, closing with `Nat.le_trans`, `Nat.add_le_mono` and `auto with arith`
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: power 2 (2*n) <= 2*n * binomial (2*n) n for n > 0

applicability.goal_shape: A goal `A < C` (or `A <= C`) where the desired bound C factors as an upper bound on an intermediate expression M and a lower bound `A <= M`, so the proof is `Nat.le_lt_trans` (or `Nat.lt_le_trans`/`Nat.le_trans`) with the intermediate `M` and two named lemmas, one per link.
applicability.use_when: the target inequality factors through a natural intermediate (here the central binomial `binomial (2*n) n`) whose lower and upper bounds are each already proved as their own lemma; the two links are non-trivial enough to deserve separate lemmas; the intermediate is something the reader can name.
applicability.avoid_when: one side of the inequality is a one-off rewrite that can be folded inline (e.g. `power 4 n <= 2*n*binomial ...` is not the point — the point is the two named bound lemmas); the intermediate does not split the goal into two reusable lemmas; the links are standard-library arithmetic that a single `auto with arith`/`lia` closes.

consequences: The move creates one obligation per link: each of the two bound lemmas must be proved before `Nat.le_lt_trans`/`Nat.lt_le_trans` compose them. Transitivity of the chain is automatic (the stdlib lemmas), but the two links must line up on the same intermediate `2 * n * binomial (2*n) n`; if the lower-bound lemma and upper-bound lemma are stated over different intermediates, the chain will not typecheck. Failure modes: a child stated too weak (e.g. the wrong exponent on `power 2` in `binomial_even`) breaks the final result, and the glue's arithmetic rewriting (`replace 4 with (power 2 2)`, the `Nat.sub_add`/`power_mult` massaging of the right-hand side) is easy to get wrong; here most of the glue is that bookkeeping, not the two applications.
